sections.html:
Rockville Centre, nicknamed RVC, is an incorporated village inside the Town of Hempstead, on Long Island's South Shore in Nassau County. It covers about 3.3 square miles of mostly dense, built-out residential blocks. The village had 26,016 residents in 2020 and an estimated 25,770 by mid-2025.

Homes are valued around $818,700, and three quarters of them (75.1 percent) are occupied by owners. A tenant pays about $1,881 a month, and the middle household earns $151,938. With values this high, even a fixer-upper represents a large sum, and carrying costs add up while a house sits.

  • 9,913 households averaging 2.55 people.
  • Monthly costs for owners with a mortgage reach the survey's top category, $4,000 or more.

sections.h2: Which school district covers my address?
sections.html:
Three districts cover the village. Most addresses belong to the Rockville Centre Union Free School District, which runs five elementary schools (Watson, Covert, Wilson, Hewitt and Riverside), South Side Middle School and South Side High School. Roughly 20 percent of village residents are in the Oceanside Union Free School District, and some live in the Baldwin district.

Because the village is small, one block can lie in a different district from the next, so the exact address matters when you price a sale. The district is printed on the school tax bill and is also asked about in the state's property disclosure form, so confirm it before listing.

The village has its own Long Island Rail Road station, and NICE buses serve it on routes n4, n15, n16, n16C and n31X. In any listing or offer discussion, state how far the house is from the station and the nearest bus stop. Buyers ask, and the answer supports your price.

The village runs its own electric and water billing, so a sale needs a few village steps beyond the usual closing papers. Water accounts pass from owner to owner, and a water closing adjustment should be done at the time of sale. Electric disconnect requests must be made in writing, with an account number and a forwarding address, and the village disconnects on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. The billing office number is 516-678-9323.

If you have been renovating, the village Building Department issues permits tied to the state building code and the village code. An open permit or an unpermitted deck can hold up the buyer's attorney, so ask the department about the status of any past work before you list.

sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bills
sections.html:
Three layers send a bill. The village collects its own tax, the Town of Hempstead's Receiver of Taxes bills general taxes and school taxes, and Nassau County, not the town, sets the assessment.

Who bills what for a Rockville Centre house
BillIssued byTiming
Village tax, second half 2026/27Village Tax OfficeMailed November 20, 2026, due January 4, 2027
General tax (town and county)Hempstead Receiver of TaxesBilled in January
School taxHempstead Receiver of TaxesBilled in October
AssessmentNassau CountySet by the county

New property owners should call the Village Tax Office at 516-678-9205 as soon as possible, so billing errors do not trigger late-payment penalties. Exemptions are removed when title transfers, so a buyer's taxes can differ a lot from yours. Hempstead also lets payers deduct 1 percent from the second-half bill when both halves of the school tax are paid by November 10, or both halves of the general tax by February 10.

sections.h2: Filing the deed with the Nassau County Clerk
sections.html:
Rockville Centre deeds are filed with the Nassau County Clerk at 240 Old Country Road in Mineola. The clerk's Land Recording Guide requires each deed to show the section, block and lot numbers on its first page, copied from the tax bill. A P.O. box is not accepted as an address.

  • The filer must include forms TP-584 and RP-5217, and nonresident sellers may also need IT-2663 for estimated income tax.
  • Transfer tax must be paid by certified check, and recording fees may be paid by personal check or card.
  • Documents should be presented at least an hour before closing.
  • Three approved e-recording companies are available to title companies and attorneys.

A deed with a wrong section, block or lot number is the most common reason for rejection. The clerk's phone number is 516-571-2664.

Sellers here usually weigh an agent, going it alone and a cash buyer. At home values near $800,000, compare each on what you net and how long it takes, not on the headline number.

  • Going through an agent exposes the house to the most buyers, but closing hinges on the buyer's mortgage and on lawyers on both sides.
  • A sale by owner skips the commission, though the state disclosure form and the village steps above fall to you.
  • A cash buyer fits a house that needs work or an estate that has to close. Insist on the price and closing date in writing.

Under Real Property Law section 462, the seller's disclosure form has to reach the buyer before a contract is signed. Its questions cover floodplains, flood insurance and basement water, which matter on a South Shore street.

sections.h2: A step-by-step plan for a village sale
sections.html:
The village layer makes an RVC sale slightly different from one in an unincorporated area, so it helps to take things in order.

  1. Find your school district on the school tax bill and note it for the listing and the disclosure form.
  2. Ask the Building Department about the status of past renovations, decks and any open permit.
  3. Call the Village Tax Office at 516-678-9205 about the village bill, and check the Hempstead bills for general and school taxes.
  4. Call the billing office at 516-678-9323 to arrange the water closing adjustment, and send the electric disconnect request in writing with an account number and a forwarding address.
  5. Give the buyer the disclosure form before a contract is signed.
  6. Have your attorney or title company prepare the deed with the section, block and lot numbers, plus the TP-584 and RP-5217, for the Nassau County Clerk.

Before you do any of it, tell the buyer's attorney early about any renovation work or village account issues. A cash sale skips the lender and the appraisal, but every item above still applies. The difference is that the closing date is set mostly by how fast these village and county steps are finished, so starting early is the best way to keep the date firm.

faqs.q: Is every Rockville Centre house in the Rockville Centre school district?
faqs.a: No. Most of the village is, but about 20 percent of residents belong to Oceanside, and part of the village falls in Baldwin. The school tax bill names your district.

faqs.q: Do I have to close my village water account when I sell?
faqs.a: Water accounts are transferred from owner to owner, and a water closing adjustment should be done at the time of sale. Call the billing office to arrange it.

faqs.q: When is the next Rockville Centre village tax payment due?
faqs.a: The second half of the 2026/27 village tax is due January 4, 2027 to avoid late penalties, and the bills are scheduled to be mailed on November 20, 2026.

faqs.q: Who sets my Rockville Centre property assessment?
faqs.a: Nassau County sets it, not the Town of Hempstead or the village. If you think the figure is too high, the town's homeowner page points to a guide on challenging an assessment.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed for a Rockville Centre sale?
faqs.a: The Nassau County Clerk in Mineola. A closing attorney or title company usually submits it, often electronically.
